title: Jimmy Noone's path from guitar to clarinet and Chicago
summary: Keppard advised Noone to switch to clarinet; Noone played with Perez and Oliver, went to Chicago and died in L.A.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I was born in Corrine. That's in Seminard Paris. And we used to go down to Merrillville, you know, they had a big store down and all the bars would be on the front gallery, you know. And he'd have the guitar playing it, you know, and we'd be dancing and going on like that. So he stayed there a while and he went and Freddie Kepard was going with his sister, you know, Sister Noon, and he advised him to put the banjo, the guitar down, and learn clarinet. So he did. Old man Chalineese is what I want to call the name that night.
I called Chalineese the other night.

Yeah. Well he was the one that learned Jimmy Noon sax, or clarinet. Clarinet? Yeah. Well then Jimmy Noon played with Freddie Wilde, he played with Manuel, and he played with Joe Oliver. Then he left and he went to Chicago, and he played with Cooks, I think it was Cook.
Yeah, for a long time. St. Cyr was with that band too.
Yeah, he played with Cook. Then after a while he organized a band of his own, Guy Kelly. Used to play with Celestine, I played with him, you know. And the last time I heard about him he died in L.A.
